title: प्रसाईका उपन्यासमा नारीअस्तित्व
nepali: बाँच्नु केवल हिँड्नु, चल्नु, सास फेर्नु, बोल्नु, खानु, मलमुत्र त्याग गर्नु मात्र होइन, आफू को हो र धर्तीमा रहेका अन्य प्राणीका तुलनामा आफ्नो स्थान र मूल्यप्रति सजग हुनु पनि हो । तर आधा आकाश ढाकेका नारीले एक्काइसौँ शताब्दीमा पनि दमन र थिचोमिचोलाई सहस्र स्विकार्दै जिएका छन् भने कतिपयले सहधर्मी पुरुषसमान जीवन जिउन पाउने अपेक्षामा असन्तुष्टि र आक्रोशको नारा पनि घन्काइरहेका छन् । नारी भएकै कारणले उत्पीडनमा परेर आफू मानव हुनुको अनुभूतिसमेत गर्न नपाइरहेको वर्तमान परिप्रेक्ष्यमा खुलेआम सडकमा उत्रनेको जमात त थपिँदै छ, यसका लागि दमित र अमुक नारीहरूलाई सचेत बनाउने र अन्यायका विरुद्ध बोल्न प्रेरित गर्ने सशक्त कारकका रूपमा साहित्यसिर्जनाको अतुलनीय भूमिका रहेको हुन्छ । यही भूमिकामा उभिएकी साहित्यकार इन्दिरा प्रसाईका उपन्यासमा तिनै अमुक नारीका अस्तित्व र पहिचानप्रतिको सचेत आवाज कसरी बुलन्द गरिएका छन् भन्ने सन्दर्भको पहिचानका लागि सिमोन द बुभाको अस्तित्ववादी नारीवादी चेतनालाई सैद्धान्तिक आधार मानी उनका हालसम्म प्रकाशित चारवटा उपन्यासमा प्रस्तुत नारीअस्तित्वसम्बन्धी चेतनाको निरूपण यसमा गरिएको छ । नारीका पहिचानप्रतिको चेतना र पितृसत्ताको विरोध एवम् लैङ्गिक विभेदप्रतिको विरोधका माध्यमबाट नारीअस्तित्वको खोजी गरिएका प्रसाईका उपन्यासले आफ्ना अधिकार र अस्तित्वका लडाईँमा सजग बनेर नारी आफैँ नउभिएसम्म कसैले उपहारका रूपमा नारीअस्तित्व र मूल्यको हिसाबकिताब नबुझाउने अभिप्रायलाई प्रस्तुत गरेको निष्कर्ष यस अध्ययनले निकालेको छ ।
american_english: Living is not merely walking, moving, breathing, speaking, eating, and excreting waste, but is also being conscious of who one is and of one's place and worth in comparison with other beings on earth. Yet women, who hold up half the sky, even in the twenty-first century live by meekly enduring suppression and oppression, while some are also raising slogans of dissatisfaction and indignation in the expectation of being able to live a life equal to that of their male counterparts. In the current context where, having fallen into oppression solely on account of being women, they are not even permitted to feel themselves to be human, the crowd of those openly taking to the streets is indeed growing, and literary creation has an incomparable role as a powerful factor in raising awareness among suppressed and anonymous women and inspiring them to speak out against injustice. Taking the existentialist feminist consciousness of Simone de Beauvoir as the theoretical foundation to identify how conscious voices regarding the existence and identity of those very anonymous women are raised in the novels of literary figure Indira Prasai, who stands in this role, the consciousness of female existence presented in her four novels published to date is examined here. This study concludes that Prasai's novels, in which the search for female existence is conducted through consciousness of women's identity, opposition to patriarchy, and resistance to gender discrimination, present the view that unless women themselves become conscious and stand up in the battle for their rights and existence, no one will hand over recognition of female existence and worth as a gift.
british_english: Living is not merely walking, moving, breathing, speaking, eating and excreting waste, but is also being conscious of who one is and of one's place and worth in comparison with other creatures on earth. Yet women, who cover half the sky, even in the twenty-first century live whilst readily accepting suppression and oppression, whilst some are also raising slogans of discontent and outrage in the expectation of being allowed to live a life equal to that of their male peers. In the present context where, having suffered oppression solely on account of being women, they are not even allowed to feel that they are human beings, the throng of those openly taking to the streets is indeed multiplying, and literary creation possesses an incomparable role as a potent catalyst in making suppressed and voiceless women aware and inspiring them to speak out against injustice. Adopting the existentialist feminist consciousness of Simone de Beauvoir as the theoretical foundation in order to determine how conscious voices concerning the existence and identity of those very anonymous women are raised in the novels of author Indira Prasai, who stands in this role, the consciousness relating to female existence presented in her four novels published to date is examined herein. This study reaches the conclusion that Prasai's novels, in which the quest for female existence is pursued through awareness of women's identity, resistance to patriarchy and opposition to gender discrimination, convey the view that unless women themselves awaken and stand up in the struggle for their rights and existence, no one will deliver recognition of female existence and worth as a gift.
australian_english: Living isn't just walking, moving, breathing, speaking, eating and passing waste, but is also being aware of who you are and of your place and worth compared with other creatures on earth. Yet women, who hold up half the sky, even in the twenty-first century live on by meekly taking suppression and oppression, while some are also shouting slogans of frustration and anger in the hope of living a life equal to their male counterparts. In the present setting where, facing oppression simply because they are women, they aren't even able to feel human, the crowd of people taking to the streets out in the open is certainly growing, and literary creation plays an unmatched part as a powerful force in waking up suppressed, nameless women and urging them to speak up against injustice. Taking the existentialist feminist consciousness of Simone de Beauvoir as the theoretical framework to see how conscious voices about the existence and identity of those same nameless women are raised in the novels of writer Indira Prasai, who fills this role, the consciousness around female existence presented in her four novels published so far is examined here. This study concludes that Prasai's novels, which pursue the search for female existence through awareness of women's identity, resistance to patriarchy and opposition to gender discrimination, put forward the idea that unless women themselves get wise and stand up in the fight for their rights and existence, nobody is going to hand over women's existence and worth as a gift.
